sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Physical Consignment of Shredded Non-Ferrous Scrap

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law system with significant Common-Law-derived commercial statutes (Private Interest Foundation regime modeled on Anglo-Caribbean offshore trust principles); unitary national legislation with no sub-state tax distinction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Active DTAAs in force: Mexico, Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Switzerland, Luxembourg, United Kingdom, UAE, Qatar, Barbados, Ireland, South Korea
BEPS-compliant treaty network per Panama's 2010-2023 tax treaty expansion program

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law 41 of 2016 and Law 129 of 2020; AML/CFT framework: Law 23 of 2015, as amended by Law 70 of 2019; DAF Resolution 62 of 2021; UBO registry: Executive Decree No. 56 of 2018 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, administered by the Direccion General de Ingresos - DGI), read with current FATF/GAFILAT standards; Panama removed from FATF grey list on 27 October 2023

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent incorporation registry in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if origin is a non-Hague state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian Resident Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if executed before a Panamanian consular office, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the founder's board authorizing creation of the Private Interest Foundation and capital endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders meeting of the founder entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passport pages and proof of residence (utility bill or bank statement) for each ultimate beneficial owner and settlor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority or residential banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille; alternatively accepted as certified CDD copies under Law 23 of 2015 client due diligence rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter confirming banking history and source of funds of the settlor and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing regulated financial institution of the settlor/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized/Apostilled or directly bank-conformed; accepted as strengthened CDD evidence for medium-risk enhanced scrap-metal scope

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory verification of every settlor, founder, UBO, protector, and controller against: (i) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) UK HMT sanctions list; (v) DAF (Panama's Financial Intelligence Unit) bulletins and Panama National Police criminal records database; (vi) Interpol notices. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence under Law 23 of 2015 (Article 35) and Law 70 of 2019, including a five-year post-office cooling-off period and source-of-wealth verification. The scrap-copper-consignment commercial model triggers the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking tier, requiring documentary LC/SWIFT TT evidence in the file and continuous transaction monitoring by the Resident Agent's AML compliance officer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Sede Electronica (online portal) - Seccion de Certificados de Vista y Denominacion Social para Fundaciones de Interes Privado
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be expressible in Latin script. Spanish and English are freely accepted; non-Latin-script names require a sworn transliteration into Latin characters accompanied by certified translation. The name must be distinctive and must not create likelihood of confusion with any existing corporation, foundation, or registered trade name in the Public Registry index; trademark conflict searches are recommended.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Panama (when used to suggest state instrumentality)
Fundacion de Interes Publico (distinct from Fundacion de Interes Privado)
Trust or Fideicomiso (when implying licensed trust operations without permit)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The licensed Resident Agent files the Vista certificate application through the Public Registry portal. If the denomination is rejected, the Resident Agent may file a 'recurso de reconsideracion' with the corresponding registral section within five business days of notification, and, if unsuccessful, a hierarchical 'recurso de apelacion' before the Director General del Registro Publico under the general administrative procedure rules aligned with Law 32 of 2016. In parallel, the applicant should reserve one or two alternative names to avoid transactional delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual statutory seat is permissible for the Private Interest Foundation: the Registered Office must be the office of the licensed Panamanian Resident Agent under Law 25 of 1995. However, the commercial operating dimension (wholesale consignment of recycled scrap copper wire) requires a physical 'Aviso de Operacion' address registered with the competent Municipality, a DGI tax activation address, and documentary substance for any future Panamanian tax residence analysis under Law 129 of 2020. Virtual occupancy of the foundation seat does not by itself satisfy the economic-substance signals of the OECD/EU for a Panamanian tax-resident trading entity; therefore the operational consignment location and records must be demonstrable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at approximately 30% during the first operational year. The scrap-metal trade is assigned to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML sector matrix in Panama, rendering DGI tax audits, Municipal Aviso de Operacion inspections, and DAF AML inspections under Law 23 of 2015 plausible; the cross-border physical consignment model and circular-metals cash/commodity flows keep the inspection probability in the mid-to-high band.

Resident Agent service agreement for the mandatory initial annual term

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), Articles 5 and 6 on the Foundation Act and patrimony, Article 7 on mandatory inscription in the Public Registry, as amended by Law No. 51 of 2015 and Law No. 11 of 2022 on transparency and beneficial ownership; subsidiary application of the Panamanian Código de Comercio for commercial operation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Panama Public Registry, Private Interest Foundations Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarized Foundation Act) together with the Reglamento (Regulations), presented for protocolization and inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Law No. 25 of 1995; nevertheless, the Foundation Act must declare the initial patrimony, which by banking market practice is fixed at no less than US$10,000 to meet know-your-customer requirements. No government escrow account is mandated; the subscribed patrimony is transferred directly to the Foundation's corporate bank account upon incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Foundation Council of the Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF, having reviewed the Foundation Act and Regulations registered with the Public Registry of Panama, hereby resolves: (1) to accept and subscribe the initial foundation patrimony of ten thousand United States dollars (US$10,000.00), fully satisfied by bank transfer to the Foundation's corporate account; (2) to adopt the statutory registered office located at the office of the Resident Agent, Panama City, Republic of Panama; (3) to ratify the appointment of the Resident Agent and of the President, Secretary and Treasurer of the Council; and (4) to open a corporate bank account, approve the AML/KYC policy prepared by the Resident Agent, and authorize the designated signatories to execute banking and commercial documentation. Resolved unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Foundation Act and Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Public Notary (Notario Público) duly licensed under the Judicial Code, acting in Panama City.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to act as Resident Agent. The attorney drafts the Escritura Pública de Fundación identifying the Founder, the Foundation name, the initial patrimony, the registered office, the initial Foundation Council, and the private Reglamento. The Founder appears before the notary personally or through a verified power of attorney, executes the instrument, and pays notarial fees and stamped-paper duties at the notary's office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Founder's passport or, if a legal entity, certificate of good standing and incumbency
Power of attorney to the Resident Agent if signing by proxy
Draft Foundation Act and Regulations approved by the Founder
Resident Agent engagement letter and AML/KYC questionnaire
Proof of address for the initial registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Founder identifies drafting defects, a corrective deed is executed and attached; any omitted mandatory clause is cured through an amendatory Foundation Act before presentation to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Protocolization and Registration at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the fully executed notarial Foundation Act and Regulations to the Private Interest Foundations Section, together with the stamped registry fee form. The Registry verifies the Founder's capacity, performs a name check, and records the inscription; the Foundation acquires legal personality upon registration. Order a certified copy of the registered Foundation Act and a Certificado de Existencia Legal for banking and licensing use.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Foundation Act and Regulations
Official registry fee payment receipt
Copy of the notarial protocol and its marginal notes
Filed power of attorney, if applicable
Certified copy of the Founder's or attorney's identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises an observation or a precautionary note, counsel files a clarifying deed and re-presents the instrument; an adverse registration decision may be appealed to the Superior Council of the Public Registry within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formalization of Governance, Corporate Books and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent's office in Panama City; Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) for beneficial-owner reporting under Law No. 23 of 2015.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the Foundation Council to pass the First Board Resolution subscribing the patrimony, adopting the registered office and appointing officers. Open the statutory minute book and the internal registry of Council members and beneficial owners. File the beneficial-owner declaration with the UAF in accordance with the 2022 transparency amendments, and maintain the verified corporate file at the Resident Agent's office.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution recorded in the original minutes
Inscribed Foundation Act and Regulations
Ultimate Beneficial Owner declaration forms under Law No. 23 of 2015
Officer identification and written acceptances
Proof of registered-office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiencies in governance records are cured by a ratification minute signed by the Council; UAF queries are resolved by resubmitting corrected beneficial-owner forms within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panamá – Ventanilla Única de Negocios.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation with the DGI to obtain the RUC for the wholesale trade of recycled non-ferrous scrap and confirm the ISIC 4669 activity code. File the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of Panama through the one-stop business window or online municipal portal, pay the municipal operating fee, and obtain the municipal operating license for the physical warehouse premises.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Foundation inscription and legal existence from the Public Registry
Certified First Board Resolution appointing officers
RUC application form filed with the DGI
Lease or title evidence of the commercial premises with zoning certificate
Identification of officers and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal refusals based on missing zoning are cured by obtaining and submitting the Certificado de Uso de Suelo; DGI objections are resolved through the taxpayer service desk with a corrected application or additional corporate documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental, Fire and Occupational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI); Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Category II Environmental Impact Report to MiAMBIENTE for the warehouse, shredding and container-loading yard. Obtain from MICI the scrap-metal wholesale operation registration and, where applicable, the export authorization for shredded copper wire. Secure the Cuerpo de Bomberos fire-safety certificate and the MITRADEL occupational health and safety program approval. Thereafter maintain monthly waste manifests, weight certificates, and export bills of lading.
required_dossiers: Municipal Aviso de Operación and RUC
Category II Environmental Impact Report with site layout
MICI scrap-metal wholesale operation and export registration forms
Fire-safety certificate and structural load certificate issued by a licensed engineer
MITRADEL occupational health and safety program
Waste management plan and annual manifests
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: MiAMBIENTE may impose mitigation conditions upon approval; if the application is rejected, supplementary environmental information is filed within the statutory cure period or an administrative appeal is lodged under the applicable environmental impact assessment regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias de Panamá (MICI) – Dirección General de Comercio Interior y Dirección General de Comercio Exterior.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Notice of Operation) and MICI Scrap-Metal Wholesale Operation License (Registro de Operación Mayorista de Metales), including any applicable scrap-copper export authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Impact Report (Informe de Impacto Ambiental), not a full EIA, because the activity is a non-smelting wholesale and transshipment depot for shredded non-ferrous scrap; a Category III full EIA would only be required if smelting, refining or hazardous-metal recovery were added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Executive Decree No. 158 of 1994 and MiAMBIENTE water-quality thresholds: BOD5 not exceeding 50 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 50 mg/L, and zero visible oil sheen in stormwater discharges. Shredded-wire dust emissions shall be controlled by bag filters so that particulate discharge does not exceed 50 mg/Nm³; scrap is screened for radioactive sources, PCBs and CFC residues; hazardous waste fractions must be disposed of exclusively through MiAMBIENTE-licensed operators with documented manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá after inspection of the warehouse, electrical installations, heat detection, extinguishers and segregated bale storage; structural load certificate signed by a licensed Panamanian engineer covering racking, mezzanine and loading-bay capacities; and workplace occupational clearance through MITRADEL's Programa de Salud Ocupacional, including risk assessment, personal protective equipment plan, and emergency response drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; e-filing and e-invoicing portal: Sistema de Información Tributaria (SIT) at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa. Customs counterpart for export clearance: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned PIF first registers under Law 25 of 1995 with the Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry) through a resident agent, stating the foundation endowment (local practice: minimum USD 100 endowment; no statutory maximum). It then obtains the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) by filing the taxpayer registration form with the DGI (in person or via SIT), attaching the foundation charter, the Public Registry certificate, the resident agent's acceptance, and identification of the foundation council members; the DGI assigns the RUC, the ISIC-based economic activity code (4669), and activates the ITBMS/VAT obligation. The PIF must also enroll in the mandatory electronic invoicing system and obtain a digital signature certificate. The statutory annual Panama PIF franchise tax (currently USD 400 under Law 52 of 2016) is payable to the National Treasury via authorized banks; foreign-source income is outside the Panamanian income tax net, but the RUC is mandatory before any Panamanian-source or export transaction is effected.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no U.S.-style check-the-box election; tax classification follows the statutory form. Relevant elections for a PIF: (i) irrevocable vs. revocable foundation status (irrevocable status fixes the foundation as the separate taxable person for Panamanian-source transactions); (ii) simplified small-taxpayer ITBMS regime election where annual turnover does not exceed USD 36,000; (iii) election of the zero-rated export treatment (rather than deemed exemption) to preserve input ITBMS refund rights; and (iv) periodic DGI refund application (devolución) for excess ITBMS credits of exporters. Panama has not enacted OECD hybrid mismatch rules; related-party transactions must be documented under Law 254 of 2021 transfer-pricing and annual information-return requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Materiales y Servicios) — Panama's VAT, regulated by Law 57 of 2007 (Tax Code Articles 1051 et seq.) as amended by Law 254 of 2021.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis exemption: any person habitually carrying out taxable transfers of goods/services in Panama must register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer regime (quarterly filing, reduced documentation) is available only where annual gross turnover does not exceed B/. 36,000 (USD 36,000). The PIF's cross-border scrap consignment is a zero-rated export supply, so full ITBMS registration (RUC + e-invoicing) is required regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all registered taxpayers (DGI Resolution 201-1197 of 2015 and phased migration completed by 2024). B2B/B2C e-invoices are issued in XML, digitally signed, timestamped and transmitted near-real-time to the DGI through an authorized fiscal service provider (Proveedor de Servicios de Facturación Electrónica); each invoice shows a QR/validation seal that the ANA and DGI cross-reference for export clearance. Export invoices must state the 0% (zero-rated) tariff code and the sale value in USD (B/.). Specified retail activities additionally require certified fiscal POS devices transmitting each transaction online; invoices not validated by the DGI cannot support an input VAT credit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A sale of recycled scrap copper wire qualifies for the 0% ITBMS rate if: (i) the seller is an RUC-registered ITBMS taxpayer with the 4669 export activity code; (ii) the goods are physically exported from Panama via a customs procedure and the Export Declaration (DUA/DEX) is accepted by the ANA; (iii) title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer; (iv) a zero-rated e-invoice is issued with the DUA reference; and (v) the purchase price is collected from abroad (documented by bank remittance or letter-of-credit settlement). Services directly related to the export (international freight, insurance, port handling) are also zero-rated. Input ITBMS suffered on domestic scrap purchases and logistics (7%) is creditable; a resulting credit balance is refundable through the DGI devolución procedure for exporters.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/DEX) accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) in the SADM/SIGA system, including any non-ferrous scrap export authorization
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill naming the PIF as consignor and the non-resident buyer as consignee
Commercial invoice and packing list with full scrap grade, weight, container count, and INCO terms
Bank remittance evidence: SWIFT MT103/MT202 or documentary letter-of-credit settlement statement evidencing receipt of proceeds from abroad
Zero-rated ITBMS e-invoice (Factura Electrónica) with DGI validation QR and tariff code 0%
Independent survey/weight certificate with moisture deduction and copper-content analysis supporting customs valuation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI reconciles zero-rated e-invoices against ANA export declarations, carrier master bills, container terminal out-gate data and bank remittance records; the standard documentary benchmark for export proceeds is 180 days from shipment. On audit, unsupported input credits are disallowed and clawed back with compensatory interest from filing date, statutory late-payment surcharge (recargo) accruing monthly, and infringement fines under the Tax Code scale (typically USD 100–USD 10,000 per offense, higher for obstruction). Fabricated export documents or DUA/DEX misdescription triggers criminal tax-fraud and smuggling sanctions under Panamanian law, including confiscation, fines and imprisonment of responsible officers, plus RUC suspension and mandatory bank guarantees for future refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank. Banking and foreign exchange activity is supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decree Law No. 9 of 1998. The US Dollar is legal tender and circulates freely; the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) exists only as coinage at an irrevocable 1:1 peg. Monetary policy is effectively delegated by the 1904 Monetary Agreement with the United States; no sovereign exchange-control authority or monetary authority creates FX rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current and capital account items. Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction: there is no exchange-control law, no approval requirement for capital entries or exits, and no restriction on current account payments. Profit remittances, dividends, and liquidation proceeds may be transferred abroad without Central Bank clearance. Practical hurdles are limited to the bank's own anti-money-laundering due diligence under Law 23 of 2015, sanctions screening, and, where Panamanian-source income is generated, documentary substantiation for withholding tax exemption (non-resident recipient). For a Private Interest Foundation conducting cross-border scrap metal trade, the capital account is unrestricted, and remittance speed is governed solely by banking compliance timelines.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panamanian law imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, conversion, or holding period for export proceeds. Recycled copper scrap exporters and trading entities may retain USD receipts in Panama, in foreign banks, or in transit; they are only subject to record-keeping requirements under the AML/CFT regime (Law 23 of 2015) and the obligation to support all payments with identifiable commercial documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-moderate. Panama has no dedicated standalone electronic money institution (EMI) license; e-money and fintech payment services operate only under SBP's Banking Law licensing or the regulatory sandbox / Fintech Innovation Hub. Offshore digital EMIs based in the UK, EU, or Hong Kong cannot open settlement accounts with Panamanian licensed banks unless they themselves are licensed or registered with the SBP, and most tier-1 banks automatically reject such clients under de-risking policies. A licensed Panamanian fintech card issuers or a corporate wallet provider can be used as a secondary collection rail, but the foundation treasury must maintain at least one primary banking relationship with a licensed bank. Recommend using global EMIs only for low-balance operating expenses while preserving the main USD liquidity in a local bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted under SBP's risk-based approach, but in practice tier-1 banks require at least one authorized signatory to appear physically at the bank's head office for a personal KYC interview. Some banks accept a remote video interview when the client is non-resident and the institution uses digital onboarding; however, a Private Interest Foundation with a non-resident founder, nominee council members, and a medium-risk scrap commodity business will generally be rated Enhanced Due Diligence, triggering an in-person meeting for the financial agent or the manager and, if flagged, for the ultimate beneficial owner. Plan for one physical visit to Panama City before the account activation and ensure that the Foundation's Registered Agent and resident director attend the meeting where possible.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk commodity sector: shredded non-ferrous scrap and copper wire classified as ISIC 4669/NAICS 423930; regulators associate this sector with cash purchases, over/under-invoicing, smuggling, and metal theft.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) product chain-of-custody log from each scrap source to the final consignment port (weighbridge certificates, container seal numbers, terminal inspection reports); (2) original commercial invoices, packing lists, and transport contracts (trucking or ocean bill of lading); (3) pre-shipment third-party inspection certificate; (4) Master Sales Agreement and Master Purchase Agreement; (5) description of the physical storage yard or port facility used; (6) complete list of counterparties and their banking references; (7) explanation of the economic function of the PIF in the physical commodity flow, supported by a one-page trade finance narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation structure: nominee council members, unrecorded beneficiaries, bearer shares in equivalent form, and maintenance of commercial activity without full corporate transparency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) certified copy of the Foundation Formation Deed (with the Business Registry stamp); (2) notarized Council Resolution appointing the treasurer or financial agent; (3) fully executed Beneficial Owner Declaration and register of beneficiaries required by Law 23 of 2015; (4) the resident agent's sworn statement evidencing the filing in Panama's Final Beneficial Owner Registry; (5) Certificate of Good Standing from the Public Registry; (6) original signatory powers and specimen signatures; (7) written explanation that the foundation is used as a special-purpose trading vehicle, not for asset concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low economic substance: a foundation managed by a resident agent, with no physical office, no staff, and no evidence of actual treasury functions in Panama.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) a Panama commercial lease or relevant physical office arrangement with utility bills; (2) the 'Aviso de Operación' municipal license for commercial trading; (3) the statutory license or notice for the scrap metal trade issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries; (4) audited or reviewed financial statements for the last two years; (5) a local accounting and tax representation agreement; (6) corporate minutes and budgetary resolutions for 2025 demonstrating active management in Panama; (7) a substance memorandum listing premises, management, assets, and the board processes in place.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment risk: consignment proceeds from non-resident buyers in higher-risk jurisdictions, unexplained third-party payors, and transactions settled before documentary confirmation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) signed trade contracts matching the invoice and the wire amount; (2) sanctions screening reports (or a contractual warranty) for all buyers, sellers, carriers, and brokers; (3) proof of the ultimate use of funds (e.g., smelter purchase order and mill acceptance certificate); (4) forward payment instructions executed on the bank's form, stating 'trade settlement – non-ferrous scrap' in the SWIFT field 70; (5) commitment to use only named beneficial owner and signatory bank accounts; (6) a letter from the foundation's legal counsel confirming that the entity has no undisclosed third-party beneficiaries.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's or lender's existing bank account in the same name as the foundation's mandated owner; use the Remittance Information field (field 70) with 'Capital Contribution – Foundation Deed No. [X] / Council Resolution [Y]' for equity, or 'Shareholder Loan – Intercompany Treasury' for debt. Panama has no statutory purpose-code list, but the beneficiary bank's compliance team expects a clear commercial description; use 'Capital contribution' or 'Trade finance advance' and cross-reference the Foundation's Registry Identification (RUC). Submit to the receiving bank in advance: (i) the Foundation Deed and latest Council Resolution, (ii) source-of-funds statement from the sending bank, (iii) the notarized beneficial owner declaration, and (iv) proof of the underlying capital call. Avoid non-mandated third-party payors; if a third-party forwarder or broker sends equity by error, the bank may freeze the sum until a notarized declaration of trust is produced.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Commercial settlements for cross-border scrap copper purchases use two primary rails: (1) Documentary Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700 (and MT707 for amendments) when the transaction requires bank risk mitigation; the credit should be irrevocable, confirmed if the foreign seller requires it, and governed by UCP 600 with payment at sight or after inspection; (2) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for commissions, freight, marine insurance, and small-value urgent payments, always with an attached commercial invoice, bill of lading, and export inspection report. For inbound documentary collections, use SWIFT MT400/MT910 collection messages to avoid open-account risk; for USD denominated transactions, Panama's banking center nets through US correspondents (CHIPS/Fedwire) and the local ACH Rail for domestic counterparties only; international outflows clear via the correspondent bank account of the chosen Panamanian clearing bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable cross-currency forward (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) for European scrap procurement
Non-deliverable FX forward (USD/CLP, USD/COP, USD/BRL, USD/MXN) via international broker for regional exposure
Cross-currency swap (USD vs EUR/GBP) for multi-year offtake or supply contracts
FX option collar (USD/EUR) on the OTC market for budgeted commodity margins
OTC call and put options on major trade currencies with an authorized Panamanian or US counterparty
COMEX/LME copper price hedge executed separately as a commodity derivative, verified through the same treasury mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax (Impuesto Anual de la Fundación) payment, evidenced by the DGI official receipt.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama; remitted through the licensed resident agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 – March 31 of each calendar year; the first payment covers the year of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 5% per month or fraction on the unpaid tax, capped at 50%; public registry certificates and reactivation procedures are denied; sustained default exposes the foundation to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) under Law 129 of 2020, confirming all ultimate natural persons holding control, 10%+ economic rights, or founder/protector positions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales; filed by the resident agent through the DGI online transparency platform.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the foundation's public registry inscription; any UBO change must be declared within 30 days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges per DGI tariff; administrative fines for omitted or false declarations; the foundation is blocked from obtaining certified documents until filing is regularized.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Panama-source Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) — required only if the foundation is assimilated to a corporation due to commercial activity generating Panama-source revenue; otherwise a zero-return is maintained to evidence territoriality.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI – Electronic Income Tax Return system (Filing Module 'Finet').
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 – March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end (calendar-year DGI window).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 5% on tax due (cap 50%), plus late-payment interest under the Código Fiscal; non-filing fines and embargo procedures; DGI assessment window of three years (extended in fraud cases).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the municipal Notice of Operations (Aviso de Operación) / local business patent — applicable only where the physical consignment activity maintains a Panama office or staffed premises.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alcaldía Municipal de Panamá (Municipal Tax Office).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year rule: January 1 – April 30 of each year (or anniversary rule per municipal ordinance).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cumulative 10% municipal surcharge per overdue year, closure order of the premises, and refusal to issue operational certificates required for export/import documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foundation Council annual meeting minutes, asset inspection, and annotation of the statutory minute book; documents retained at the registered office and made available to the UAF/DGI upon request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the foundation (no governmental filing); subject to inspection by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), DGI, and judicial authorities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (by March 31) or per the terms of the foundation charter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fiduciary default of the Foundation Council; missing records can invalidate asset-protection claims in fraudulent-conveyance disputes and impede documentary credit/LC documentation requirements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit for a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. Mandatory independent IFRS audit is triggered only if: (a) the foundation engages in commercial activities and is assimilated to a corporation for fiscal purposes under Art. 17 of Law 25; (b) the trade-finance bank or LC issuing institution imposes an audit covenant; or (c) a shareholder/beneficiary dispute requires court-ordered audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama/IFRS for SMEs (Law 11 of 1999; Código de Comercio) for consolidated or commercial books; Law 25 of 1995 Art. 22 requires the foundation to maintain accounting records reflecting assets, liabilities, and operations under generally accepted accounting principles in Panama.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 129 of 2020, the resident agent must submit the annual UBO confirmation within 30 days of the foundation's anniversary and within 30 days of any change to the ultimate beneficial ownership (transfers of economic rights from shareholdings or discriminatory entitlements). The foundation must maintain a contemporaneous registry of any transfer of economic entitlements and notify the agent immediately; failures are penalized by DGI fines and suspension of certifications.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of the Founder and initial endowment (Derecho de Aplicación)
Register of Foundation Council members (equivalent to Register of Directors)
Register of Protector and supervisory authorities
Minute book (Foundation Council actas) and full accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 7,500 per year (audit is voluntary unless commercial-activity assimilation or LC banking covenant)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: income derived from foreign-source trading operations is outside the Panamanian tax net if title transfer and economic activity occur abroad. Preferential 15% rate applies to the first USD 50,000 of Panamanian-source taxable income; the excess is taxed at 25%. A Private Interest Foundation that limits its activities to foreign-source asset holding and export title transfers faces an effective zero rate on those earnings and pays only the annual PIF statutory fee of USD 300.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 138 (Declaración Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the e-Tax 2.0 portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) at https://etax.mef.gob.pa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The fiscal year is the accounting period used by the entity; for calendar-year entities the return covers the 1 January – 31 December period unless the DGI approves a different fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end, with no general extension. A calendar-year taxpayer must file no later than 31 March. If the statutory date falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to the next ordinary business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, taxpayer registration number (RUC), fiscal year, tax domicile and registered agent address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an investor-owned PIF with no Panama-source operations, confirm the 'no local commercial activity' indicator and enter the registered agent address in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian-source commercial activities, sales of goods, services, rents, or other locally generated revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude all foreign-source income from cross-border scrap copper transactions where title, risk, and delivery pass outside Panama; input zero if the PIF has only extraterritorial trading revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 225 – Cost of sales and operating deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions directly attributable to Panama-source income, supported by invoices, bills of lading, and contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses connected with Panamanian taxable income. Foreign purchase costs of recycled scrap and freight costs related to non-Panama-source revenue must be excluded from the Form 138 calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after permissible deductions and fiscal adjustments; the base used for the 15%/25% rate schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF with no Panamanian taxable income, enter zero. Do not offset foreign-source losses against Panama-source profits without a recognized DGI allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 301 – Tax charged and net tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the tax at 15% on the first USD 50,000 of net taxable income and 25% on the excess; deduct prepayments, credits, and anticipos to arrive at the balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source taxable base exists, insert zero and attach the annual PIF fee payment proof if relying on Law 25 of 1995 exemption provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due per month or fraction, capped at 50%, plus monthly interest of 1.5% on the overdue tax. Zero-return late filers face fixed administrative fines of USD 50 to USD 500. Persistent non-filing triggers DGI automatic assessment, suspension of the RUC, penalty duplication, and criminal referral when the omission is fraudulent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% of gross dividends paid by a Panamanian company to resident or non-resident shareholders. Dividends charged to profits already subjected to Panamanian corporate income tax benefit an effective 5% reduced withholding; dividends derived wholly from foreign-source activities may be outside the withholding regime under the territoriality principle.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Panamanian withholding agent before remittance: (i) a certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the treaty-state tax authority, (ii) a sworn beneficial-ownership declaration, and (iii) the DTA entitlement analysis. The withholding agent uploads the supporting file through e-Tax 2.0 under the double-taxation convention module and retains the TRC for six years. DGI may issue a specific ruling applying the treaty rate; refunds for excess withholding are recovered through the annual income tax return. Panama's limited DTA network (Mexico, Barbados, Qatar, UAE) generally reduces dividend withholding to 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalties for Panamanian-source IP use and technical assistance are subject to 15% final withholding tax; DTA rates generally lower this to 10%. Interest paid to non-resident lenders on Panamanian-source loans is subject to 10% withholding, reduced to 5% under applicable DTAs; interest on qualifying cross-border bank financing may be exempt if the lender has no local permanent establishment and the loan is registered with the Central Bank of Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 3,000,000 gross annual income in the preceding fiscal year or aggregate related-party transactions above USD 500,000 triggers the mandatory Form 233 and Local File. A Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds USD 50,000,000. All thresholds are in US dollars, which is the de facto and legal transactional currency in Panama (Balboa pegged 1:1 to USD).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under Executive Decree No. 133 of 2021 apply to Panamanian juridical persons carrying out 'Relevant Activities' such as distribution and service centres, headquarters, financing, insurance, IP-holding, and shipping. A PIF engaged in cross-border physical consignment and trading of recycled scrap copper wire is not automatically exempt: if the foundation performs management, purchasing, and logistical coordination from Panama, it will be treated as a distribution centre and must evidence local office premises, full-time employees, board-management meetings in Panama, and proportionate operating expenditure. Passive asset-holding foundations are excluded, but active commodity traders require an annual ESR filing and may be sanctioned for insufficient substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting scrap copper sales revenue, issuing or accepting false export invoices, overstating cost of sales, or claiming fictitious deductions for a PIF that is actually carrying on commercial activity in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine equal to twice the amount of tax evaded. Civil tax assessment adds the underpaid tax, a 25% surcharge, monthly interest at 1.5%, and suspension or cancellation of the RUC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and foundation council members who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalties, and interest. A court can order preventive seizure of personal assets, restrict re-entry or travel bans, and impose imprisonment for the fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the PIF as a paper vehicle that routes scrap-copper purchase and sale agreements through Panama without local employees, physical office, or management decision-making, solely to claim an exemption or treaty benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR non-compliance penalties up to USD 100,000 for non-filing or false certification; the DGI may disregard the entity and recharacterize the transactions as Panama-source income subject to 25% corporate income tax plus a 10% surcharge. Registry-level sanctions may include cancellation of the PIF enrollment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is permitted in deliberate substance abuse; foundation council members can be held personally liable for restitution of the evaded tax and for wrongful signature of the substance declaration. Travel restrictions may be imposed pending criminal tax proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using mismatched Swift TT or documentary LC flows, nominee bank accounts, split payments, or inaccurate bills of lading to wash proceeds from the sale of recycled copper wire while falsifying cargo descriptions, weight, or origin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 17 of 2022 range from USD 100,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation, plus asset confiscation. Money laundering as a criminal predicate carries imprisonment of 3 to 10 years and disqualification from commercial activity in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director or foundation council member who knowingly facilitates layering through letters of credit or wire transfers faces personal criminal liability, travel bans, and freezing of personal and foundation assets. The corporate veil is pierced for sham transactions, and overseas extradition may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excluding intercompany charges from the recyclable copper supply chain, applying a margin that deviates from the CME/LME copper reference price without justification, or failing to file Form 233 when related-party transactions exceed the legal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may impose a transfer-pricing adjustment plus a 10% surcharge and late-payment interest; penalties for non-filing of Form 233 range from USD 500 to USD 20,000, increasing for repeat violations and for multinational groups participating in aggressive pricing schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors whose false pricing certification causes the corporation to receive a tax benefit are jointly liable for the corrected tax and sanctions. In egregious cases, deliberate transfer-pricing manipulation is prosecuted as tax evasion, exposing directors to imprisonment and civil restitution orders.
